teaser: Two agent teams, one night: RC1 of the book of The Ultimate Insider, a cold read by a team that knew only the record, and a companion PDF of tick boxes.
core_idea: A book can now be made like a release: one team that knows everything builds the register, timeline and plan, a second team reads the same record cold, the book is drafted from the signed plan in an hour with every number tied to a register id, and a companion PDF turns every role's review into a card pinned to a sentence and a page, with boxes to tick, so one author with a pen can take every decision on a flight and the ticks become data.

nodes.label: Two teams on one record
nodes.summary: One team knows everything, a second knows only the record.

nodes.label: The cold read
nodes.summary: Thirteen agents, one commit, every claim cited or marked unknown.

nodes.label: Every number has an id
nodes.summary: RC1's numbers come from the claims register, C001 to C042.

nodes.label: RC1
nodes.summary: 294 pages at 6 by 9 inches, built about an hour after the plan was signed.

nodes.label: The companion
nodes.summary: 67 A4 pages, 98 cards, each pinned to a sentence and a page of RC1.

nodes.label: A review as a form
nodes.summary: Decisions with boxes, questions with lines: answered on paper, turned into data.

nodes.label: Rebuilt to the pixel
nodes.summary: A second session rebuilt both PDFs and matched them page for page.

nodes.label: Three findings, no secrets
nodes.summary: The values the reviews found were anonymous cookies and form tokens.

nodes.label: A book is now a release
nodes.summary: A version, a hash, a gate and a rerunnable build, between a signature and a flight.

quotes.text: The companion turns the pile into a form.
one team that knows everything, one that knows only the record, and the book written from where they meet.
quotes.why: The method for books from now on.

quotes.text: A book is now a release.
